Prepare one row per estimated dog from the 2024 NYC licenses. Keep the recorded name beside the spelling used for matching and report missing names separately.

## Packages and helpers
```{r}
library(tidyverse)
source("R/helpers.R")
```

## From licenses to estimated dogs
### Read the license records
NYC supplies the column headers. We read ZIP codes as text because a leading zero is part of the code and matters when joining to the income data. Reading the other fields as text also keeps names as written, including the two letters `NA` used for a missing name.
```{r}
#| label: read-license-records
sources <- read_csv("data/sources.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
dogs_raw <- read_csv(
  "data/raw/nyc-dogs-2024.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()),
  na = character(), trim_ws = FALSE
)
missing_labels <- read_csv(
  "data/lookups/missing_name_labels.csv",
  col_types = cols(.default = col_character()), na = character()
)
```

### Give the original license fields clear names
The city calls the dog’s name `animalname`. We call it `original_name` to keep the recorded spelling beside the matching spelling. Breed and sex get short names. The row number identifies the source license.
```{r}
#| label: name-license-columns
dogs_raw |>
  rename(
    original_name = animalname,
    sex = animalgender,
    birth_year = animalbirth,
    breed = breedname,
    original_zipcode = zipcode,
    license_issue_date = licenseissueddate,
    license_expiry_date = licenseexpireddate
  ) |>
  mutate(source_row_id = row_number()) ->
  dogs_original
```

```{r}
#| label: preview-original-licenses
dogs_original |>
  preview()
```

### Identify missing names
Our lookup lists six ways the city recorded a missing name, including `UNKNOWN` and `NA`. We match them before changing any spelling. We keep `BABY` as a name.
```{r}
#| label: label-missing-names
dogs_original |>
  left_join(missing_labels, by = c("original_name" = "recorded_name")) |>
  mutate(
    name_status = replace_na(name_status, "recorded"),
    name_missing = name_status == "not_recorded"
  ) ->
  dogs_with_name_status
```

### Format names for matching
Uppercase the whole name, then remove spaces and hyphens. These are the spelling differences we agreed to ignore when matching. For example, `WALL-E` becomes `WALLE`. Preserve the recorded name so compounds can still be identified.
```{r}
#| label: format-names
dogs_with_name_status |>
  mutate(name = str_to_upper(original_name, locale = "en")) |>
  mutate(name = str_remove_all(name, "[\\s-]")) ->
  dogs_with_matching_names
```

### Format ZIP codes
If a ZIP contains one to five digits, pad it to five digits with leading zeros. `str_detect()` checks the digits and `str_pad()` supplies the zeros. This prepares the ZIP for the geography join.
```{r}
#| label: format-zipcodes
dogs_with_matching_names |>
  mutate(
    zipcode_contains_one_to_five_digits = str_detect(original_zipcode, "^[0-9]{1,5}$"),
    zipcode_with_leading_zeros = str_pad(original_zipcode, width = 5, pad = "0")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    zipcode = if_else(zipcode_contains_one_to_five_digits, zipcode_with_leading_zeros, original_zipcode)
  ) ->
  dogs_with_zipcodes
```

### Read license dates
The source dates include a time. Take the first ten characters, such as `2024-05-30`, and read them as dates so we can sort the licenses.
```{r}
#| label: read-license-dates
dogs_with_zipcodes |>
  mutate(
    license_issue_date = str_sub(license_issue_date, 1, 10),
    license_expiry_date = str_sub(license_expiry_date, 1, 10)
  ) |>
  mutate(
    license_issue_date = parse_date(license_issue_date),
    license_expiry_date = parse_date(license_expiry_date),
    extract_year = as.integer(extract_year)
  ) ->
  dogs_with_dates

dogs_with_dates |>
  select(original_name, name, original_zipcode, zipcode, license_issue_date) |>
  preview()
```

### Flag uncertain fields
We flag compounds using the spelling on the license. We also mark records with an unknown breed or sex, a questionable birth year or a ZIP that cannot be written as five digits. These licenses still count.

```{r}
#| label: flag-uncertain-fields
dogs_with_dates |>
  mutate(
    breed_label = str_trim(breed),
    birth_year_number = as.integer(birth_year)
  ) |>
  mutate(breed_label = str_to_upper(breed_label)) |>
  mutate(
    name = if_else(name_missing, NA_character_, name),
    compound_name = !name_missing & str_detect(original_name, "\\S\\s+\\S|[^\\s-]-[^\\s-]"),
    zipcode_padded = zipcode != original_zipcode,
    zipcode_invalid = !str_detect(zipcode, "^[0-9]{5}$"),
    breed_unknown = breed_label %in% c("", "UNKNOWN"),
    birth_year_has_four_digits = str_detect(birth_year, "^[0-9]{4}$"),
    birth_year_in_range = between(birth_year_number, 1990L, 2024L),
    birth_year_suspect = !birth_year_has_four_digits | !birth_year_in_range,
    birth_year_suspect = replace_na(birth_year_suspect, TRUE),
    sex_unknown = !sex %in% c("F", "M")
  ) |>
  mutate(
    identity_uncertain = breed_unknown | birth_year_suspect | sex_unknown | zipcode_invalid
  ) ->
  dogs_with_quality_flags
```

### Select named records
We use named licenses to estimate individual dogs. We report missing names separately by ZIP using all licenses.

```{r}
#| label: select-named-records
dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  filter(!name_missing) ->
  named_licenses
```

### Estimate individual dogs
We treat licenses with the same full name after formatting, sex, birth year, breed and ZIP as one estimated dog. Within each group, we sort the newest issue date first. A tie goes to the later expiry date, then to the earlier row in the source file. `slice_head(n = 1)` keeps the first license in each sorted group. `license_record_count` records how many licenses that row represents. For example, the two matching TOTORO licenses were issued in 2019 and 2024. The 2024 row represents both.

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs
dog_key <- c("name", "sex", "birth_year", "breed", "zipcode")
named_licenses |>
  group_by(name, sex, birth_year, breed, zipcode) |>
  mutate(
    license_record_count = n(),
    original_name_variants = n_distinct(original_name),
    any_compound_name = any(compound_name),
    latest_issue_date = max(license_issue_date),
    latest_issue_ties = sum(license_issue_date == latest_issue_date)
  ) |>
  arrange(desc(license_issue_date), desc(license_expiry_date), source_row_id, .by_group = TRUE) |>
  slice_head(n = 1) |>
  ungroup() |>
  mutate(
    retained_row_label = str_pad(source_row_id, width = 6, pad = "0"),
    estimated_dog_id = str_c("dog2024-", retained_row_label)
  ) |>
  arrange(source_row_id) ->
  dogs_estimated
```

```{r}
#| label: estimate-individual-dogs-preview
dogs_estimated |>
  select(estimated_dog_id, original_name, license_record_count) |>
  preview()
```

### Keep the dog fields
```{r}
#| label: select-dog-fields
dogs_estimated |>
  select(
    estimated_dog_id, source_row_id, extract_year, original_name, name,
    sex, birth_year, breed, original_zipcode, zipcode,
    license_issue_date, license_expiry_date, license_record_count,
    original_name_variants, latest_issue_ties, compound_name, any_compound_name,
    breed_unknown, birth_year_suspect, sex_unknown, zipcode_padded, zipcode_invalid,
    identity_uncertain
  ) ->
  dogs
```

### Trace source records to dogs
Keep a row-by-row explanation of which source records were consolidated or lacked a name.
```{r}
#| label: trace-source-records-to-dogs
dogs |>
  select(all_of(dog_key), estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id = source_row_id) ->
  dog_identity_lookup

dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  left_join(dog_identity_lookup, by = dog_key) |>
  mutate(
    record_status = case_when(
      name_missing ~ "missing_name",
      source_row_id == retained_source_row_id ~ "retained",
      TRUE ~ "consolidated"
    )
  ) |>
  select(source_row_id, estimated_dog_id, retained_source_row_id, record_status) ->
  license_to_dog
```

### Summarize source missingness
Each license contributes once to the missing-name share for its ZIP.
```{r}
#| label: summarize-source-missingness
dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  group_by(extract_year, zipcode) |>
  summarise(
    source_license_records = n(), missing_name_records = sum(name_missing),
    named_license_records = sum(!name_missing),
    missing_name_share = mean(name_missing), .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  arrange(zipcode) ->
  missing_by_zip

dogs_with_quality_flags |>
  filter(name_missing) |>
  count(original_name, name = "source_license_records", sort = TRUE) ->
  missing_name_counts
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-source-missingness-preview
missing_name_counts
```

### Summarize quality flags
```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags
quality_flags <- c("breed_unknown", "birth_year_suspect", "sex_unknown",
  "zipcode_padded", "zipcode_invalid", "identity_uncertain", "compound_name")
named_licenses |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "named_license_record") ->
  license_quality_counts

dogs |>
  summarise(across(all_of(quality_flags), sum)) |>
  mutate(unit = "estimated_dog") ->
  dog_quality_counts

license_quality_counts |>
  bind_rows(dog_quality_counts) |>
  pivot_longer(cols = all_of(quality_flags), names_to = "flag", values_to = "count") |>
  select(unit, flag, count) ->
  quality_summary
```

```{r}
#| label: summarize-quality-flags-preview
quality_summary
```

## Save the prepared dogs
```{r}
#| label: save-dogs
# Create the folder for these tables if needed.
dir.create("data/derived", showWarnings = FALSE)
write_csv(dogs, "data/derived/dogs_prepared_2024.csv", na = "")
write_csv(license_to_dog, "data/derived/license_to_dog.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_by_zip, "data/derived/missing_names_by_zip.csv", na = "")
write_csv(missing_name_counts, "data/derived/missing_name_labels.csv", na = "")
write_csv(quality_summary, "data/derived/quality_flags.csv", na = "")
```

Different dogs can share all five identifying fields. A change in a dog’s recorded details can also split its licenses into several groups. These are estimates of individual dogs.
